Nothing needed fixing this run, but 12 of the 32 CPU cores are idle because both queues are empty.

- **Running:** 5 FEBio runs: physF4_p060, physF4_p083, physF4dt_p060, physF4dt_p061 and physF4dt_p083. Each log was updated within the last 12 s, and model time is at 3.62–3.83. Each run is on 4 separate cores with no threads doubled up on one core.
- **Finished since 10:28:** physF4_p062, physF4dt_p062 and physF4_p061. All three show exit 0 and `normal: True` in their `.out` files, so they are not FEBio errors hidden behind a clean exit code.
- **Resources:** 18.1 of 32 cores in use. Memory is 117.6 of 137.4 GB, but only 15.9 GB is real program memory; the rest is file cache. Nothing has been killed for lack of memory. GPUs 1–4 hold my runs at 0 % use; GPUs 0, 5 and 6 belong to other users.
- **Queues:** the FEBio queue has 0 waiting, 5 running, 2568 done and 2 old failures. The task queue has 0 queued and 0 running; the 5 failed `gate2_*` tasks are unchanged.
- **Services:** all the tmux services are up, and the keepalive is getting HTTP 200 every 10 minutes.
- **Actions:** none. The idle cores can't go to the running jobs: a run's thread count is fixed when it starts, so adding threads means restarting it and losing progress.

**Needs a person:** someone has to queue the next decided work (FEBio runs in `human_study/queue`, Python jobs in `work/ops/tasks/queue`), or everything will sit idle once these 5 runs finish. Someone also needs to decide whether to re-queue the 5 `gate2_*` tasks.
